statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail falls back from 15 to 8 because the cash-open downside leg has been fully retraced: NQ has recovered about 180 points from the 29,425 session low and trades above its previous close, while stress stays high across the energy, rates and trade channels.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with a narrow flagged window from 17:00 to 18:00 UTC around the US 3-year note auction, the one scheduled checkpoint able to reactivate the rates channel that accompanied the morning decline. Tail sits well below the block threshold because mean reversion has demonstrably worked this session rather than failed.
headline: NQ round-trips the cash-open decline back above its previous close as semiconductors gain 2% while the Dow holds a 1% loss
body: NQ futures trade near 29,605.50, up 0.14% on the session, after a full round trip inside the 29,425.00 to 29,764.75 day range. Price has recovered roughly 180 points from the session low reported an hour ago and now sits above the 29,544 prior close, so the directional downside leg that lifted tail to 15 last hour has been retraced rather than extended. That is the reason tail falls back to 8: the specific structure that matters here is repeated extension after failed retracements, and the opposite occurred. The cash index confirms it, with the Nasdaq-100 at 29,592.61, up 0.16%, inside a 29,400.70 to 29,655.73 range, so the index is in the upper half of its range rather than near the low. Volatility is decaying with the recovery. VIX at 15.36 is up only 0.39% and sits near the bottom of its 15.30 to 15.94 day range, having given back the earlier spike. The rates channel has also stopped tightening: the 10-year yield at 4.784% is mid-range between 4.760% and 4.796% rather than pinned at the high, and the H.15 release for 3 September had the 2-year at 4.34% against the 10-year at 4.77%. Index internals remain sharply split, which is what keeps the dominant mode at mixed rather than trend-up. SOXX is up 2.10% at 530.78 after Qualcomm's multi-generation custom-silicon agreement with Amazon, while the Dow is down 0.99% at 52,883.69 near the lower end of its 52,721.62 to 53,110.45 range. That is rotation into semiconductors against cyclical weakness, not broad one-way index pressure. Stress stays in the high band at 69, easing only marginally from 72. WTI near $93.00 is up 1.66% and Brent near $98.06 is up 0.93%, at roughly three-month highs after further Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure that suspended operations at several facilities, and the outage duration is unresolved. Canada's retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on U.S. goods took effect today, keeping the North American trade channel live. The one scheduled release inside the current hour has already printed: the New York Fed's August Survey of Consumer Expectations, published at 15:00 UTC, showed one-year inflation expectations unchanged at 3.6%, the three-year measure down to 3.2%, the five-year measure at 3.0%, and mean unemployment expectations at 44.4%, the highest since April 2020. Steady inflation expectations alongside a weaker labour-market read is a benign combination for the rates channel and is consistent with the observed recovery. The next scheduled checkpoint is the US 3-year note auction at 17:00 UTC, which is the flagged window. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 12:18 UTC and is outside the 90-minute freshness limit, so this assessment rests on the independently fetched live sources listed below rather than on that delayed snapshot.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the assessment stayed in the EA_ON band with tail between 5 and 10 until the 14:00 UTC slot, where it stepped up to 15 on an observed cash-open downside leg that left NQ near the session low. Stress climbed steadily from the low 60s during Monday's Labor Day holiday session to 72 by early Tuesday afternoon as crude extended on the Saudi facility strikes and the North American trade channel reopened. The dominant mode sat at mixed for most of the window because cross-asset signals kept diverging from Nasdaq price action, turning to trend-down only for the single hour that carried the decline. The 09:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The horizon starts with the cash-open decline fully retraced and conditional tail back at 8, then steps up modestly around the 17:00 UTC 3-year auction and again into the 20:00 UTC closing auction, where rebalancing flow meets wide sector dispersion. Conditional tail falls to the floor of the horizon overnight through the Asian session, with the 07:00 UTC European open on 9 September and the 13:30 UTC US cash open as the next flow checkpoints; the second of those carries the horizon peak because opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure that overwhelms mean reversion. Every slot stays inside the EA_ON band. Two channels could force a step change in either direction: Middle East energy headlines, where the duration of the Saudi refinery outages is unresolved, and the North American trade dispute after Canada's tariffs took effect today. Stress stays in the high band throughout because neither channel is resolved, while confidence decays overnight as the live evidence base ages and recovers once the 9 September cash session provides fresh structure.

forecast.analysis: Observed now: the cash-open decline has been fully retraced. NQ trades near 29,606, back above the 29,544 prior close after a 180-point recovery from 29,425, and the Nasdaq-100 sits at 29,593 inside a 29,401-29,656 range. VIX has eased to 15.36 near its day low. Mean reversion worked, so tail drops from 15 to 8.

Nasdaq-100 at 29,593, back above the 29,544 previous close
VIX 15.36, near the low end of its 15.30-15.94 day range

NY Fed August survey released at 15:00 UTC with steady inflation expectations

forecast.analysis: The US 3-year note auction settles at 17:00 UTC and is the flagged checkpoint. With the 10-year at 4.784% inside a 4.760-4.796% range, a weak auction tail would push yields toward the day high and is the most plausible route to a second equity leg. Conditional tail steps up modestly rather than blocking, since no such leg is observed.

10-year yield 4.784%, mid-range but close to the 4.796% day high
Rates were the channel that accompanied the earlier downside leg
A well-covered auction would instead remove a pressure source

forecast.analysis: Post-auction digestion. If the 17:00 UTC auction clears without a yield spike, the rates channel that accompanied the morning decline loses force and conditional tail eases back. The scenario that would keep it elevated is repeated extension in the direction the auction sets, which cannot be judged before the result is known.
drivers: Yield reaction to the 3-year auction is the main input this hour
Retracement behaviour so far this session argues against one-way extension
Energy headlines remain the main out-of-calendar interrupt
Stress stays anchored high by Brent near $98

The hour matters more as the approach to the closing auction: conditional tail is held rather than raised, because a late trend normally needs an already-directional afternoon, which the observed round trip has not produced.
drivers: Consumer Credit Change (Jul) at 19:00 UTC, limited index transmission
Positioning ahead of the 20:00 UTC US cash close
Dow-versus-Nasdaq dispersion has persisted through the session
No repeated extension after failed retracements observed so far

forecast.analysis: Closing-auction hour, the highest-imbalance window of the US session. Conditional tail carries its small session peak here because month-of-September rebalancing flows and a heavy energy-versus-tech dispersion can produce a fast late leg. It remains far below the block threshold given today's demonstrated retracement.
drivers: US cash close at 20:00 UTC concentrates imbalance flow
Wide sector dispersion raises the size of any rebalancing print
Late-session continuation risk is a checkpoint, not an observed path
Brent near $98 keeps the energy-versus-tech split in place

Liquidity drops sharply and index futures usually revert to range behaviour, so conditional tail returns to the low band and stress eases with realised volatility. Confidence steps down because the live evidence base thins once cash trading ends and only futures price discovery remains.

Evidence base narrows to NQ futures once cash is closed
Any late headline has an outsized effect in thin books
Stress declines with the volume, not with the underlying catalysts

Conditional tail sits at the horizon floor because thin, catalyst-free hours rarely sustain the persistent no-retracement structure that matters here. The stated scores assume no new energy or geopolitical headline arrives, which is the main invalidation.

Thin evening futures books favour range behaviour
Middle East headline flow is the main invalidation for this hour

Energy is the channel to watch overnight: further reporting on Saudi refinery outages would reprice crude first and reach index futures only indirectly.

A gap in Japanese or Korean semiconductor names would be the first sign that the Qualcomm-driven chip strength is being repriced regionally.

This hour is included as a continuation checkpoint: if NQ is still holding the recovered level here, the case that the session's decline was a one-off leg strengthens for the European handover.
drivers: Quietest liquidity window of the 24-hour horizon
Holding the recovered level here would confirm the retracement
No scheduled catalyst in this window

forecast.analysis: Late Asian hours. Scores are unchanged because nothing in the calendar distinguishes this hour, and the assumption remains orderly two-way trade. The stated risk would only change if crude gapped on fresh supply news, which is a conditional path and not something observed at the assessment cutoff.
drivers: No scheduled release differentiates this hour

Range behaviour assumed to persist through the Asian close
Stress held in the elevated band by unresolved energy risk

forecast.analysis: Asian close approaches. Conditional tail remains at the floor of the horizon. The relevant checkpoint is whether the Asian session hands over a flat or a directional book to Europe; a flat handover is assumed here, consistent with the contained overnight behaviour of recent sessions.

Flat handover assumed rather than observed
Confidence enters the solid band as live evidence ages further

If instead NQ has trended in one direction through the whole Asian session by this point, that would be the first genuine amplifier of the horizon and would invalidate the floor-level conditional tail shown here.

Neither move reflects observed structure; both reflect the routine widening of ranges as European participants price the prior US session.

Overnight positioning adjustments widen ranges mechanically

Any observed one-way pressure into the open would need to be confirmed by a later assessment before it justified a higher tail reading.

Whether NQ follows that split is a scenario, not an observation.
